text:
anya: Hey team — I'm blocked merging my docs PR for the embeddings endpoint. CI preview deployed but runtime wants a clear statement of how multipart inputs are handled (I added two example snippets that assume different behavior). @liam @erin can you confirm what the API actually does when you send an array of text parts as one item?

docs-bot: Preview available: https://deploy-preview-289.docs.redwood.ai (:eyes:)

liam: We currently treat the array of strings for one item as 'concatenate with a single space' then compute one embedding for the combined text. So request -> single vector.

olivia: Quick add — there was a failing test in the runtime suite: when all parts are empty strings it used to return an empty vector, which broke some clients.

liam: Yes — that was a bug. We changed behavior: if the combined text length == 0 we return 400 with a short error message ("empty input"). I'll push the unit test change later today.

anya: Great. So docs should show the single-embedding case. I also added an example that passes an array-of-items (batch) where each item is itself an array of strings — is that valid? i.e., nested arrays like [["a","b"],["c"]] -> do we accept that shape?

erin: Hmm the SDK examples currently show embeddings.create(inputs=["one","two"]) and the REST docs show items: ["..."]. We need exact wording to avoid confusion.

liam: We do NOT accept nested arrays. The server expects a batch (array) of items, where each item is either a string or an array of strings (to be concatenated). But we do not accept items that are arrays of arrays. If a client posts nested arrays we return 422 with an error explaining unsupported shape.

olivia: CI preview flagged the nested-array example — that's why the PR is blocked.

anya: Ok that explains it. I will remove the nested-array example. Can someone paste the exact 422 error schema/message to include in the docs?

liam: Use this snippet for the response body:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 422,
    "message": "unsupported input shape: nested arrays are not accepted; use array of strings per item or plain string",
    "type": "invalid_request"
  }
}
```

erin: Perfect. Also add a small note about batching semantics: "When sending multiple items in a single request, each item yields one embedding. If an item is an array of strings, those strings are concatenated with a single space before embedding." I'll update the PR text and examples accordingly.

anya: One more tiny edge case: does concatenation insert a space even if a part ends with punctuation? e.g., ["Hello.", "World"] -> "Hello. World"?

liam: Yes, we insert exactly one ASCII space between parts regardless of punctuation; that's stable across model backends.

olivia: Filed a follow-up e2e: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/embeddings-e2e/452 — flaky when parts had trailing spaces. We should call out that leading/trailing whitespace is preserved before join.

liam: Good point — preserve whitespace, then join with single space. So example in docs should show trimming guidance if you want to normalize.

anya: Ok I'll add a note and example showing `.strip()` in python snippet.

erin: Once you push the change I'll remove the hold and merge after green CI.

anya: Pushed update: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4826 — removed nested-array example, added 422 snippet, clarified concat behavior and empty-input 400.

deploy-bot: docs PR 4826 preview redeployed: https://deploy-preview-4826.docs.redwood.ai (:white_check_mark:)

erin: I reviewed and left one tiny copy tweak, but nothing blocking. Removing hold now.

anya: Thanks all, merging after final CI.

deploy-bot: PR merged to main by anya — changelog updated. :tada:
